expected: Claude did well at organizing my letter around the same two areas as my original: measurable performance improvements and real-time spatial computing. It connected my Phoebe experience to Roblox’s engineering articles and kept the token and rendering results tied to their test conditions. However, the long performance paragraph reads like my résumé bullets joined together, and phrases such as “a mentor to argue with” are too casual for this application. It also incorrectly claims that both spatial projects used Python and C++, and exaggerates the evidence by saying my evaluations made the Phoebe changes safe. I would keep the two-area structure and relevant company research while removing unsupported claims and giving Phoebe and Coach Bob more room to explain why the work matters. This experience showed me that AI can be useful for organizing a first draft, identifying connections between my experience and a job posting, and suggesting clearer wording. It can also help me notice repetition or gaps that I miss when reviewing my own writing. I would not use it to recite accomplishments since it seems to still hallucinate, explain technical work it does not understand, or write personal reflections that I dont actually stand behind. Submitting its output without checking it could leave me defending claims in an interview that are inaccurate or not mine which is not a good look for any job. For job applications, I see AI as an editing partner and tool to get from nothing to first draft but not to a submittable final version. I should remain responsible for the facts, the voice, and the final decisions so the application represents someone I can confidently be in the interview.
